audit_findings.title: Positive-growth cases may omit the reinvestment needed to produce that growth
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 working-capital cash use of $37.6 million; base and bull operating values exceed bear by $85 million and $184 million, respectively
audit_findings.mechanism: Required working capital and growth capex reduce projected owner earnings supporting the 3% and 6% growth cases.
audit_findings.evidence: Working capital used $37.6 million of cash due to a $36.5 million increase in inventories and a $20.4 million increase in accounts receivable partially offset by a $19.3 million increase in accounts payable and accrued expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates substantial working-capital investment, but does not establish that the entire $37.6 million is recurring. The supplied valuation does not show how its 14.9% RONTA assumption translates growth into reinvestment deductions. Because the unsupported positive-growth increments produce values of $28.70 and $33.65 per share versus a $31.26 price, an adequate reinvestment charge could change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct each forecast year using growth divided by the 14.9% RONTA as required incremental operating investment, distinguish working capital from maintenance and growth capex, and rerun the base and bull cases.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may normalize a volatile steel spread at an unsustainably favorable level
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 gross-profit improvement from spreads was $36.1 million, equal to 91.9% of the $39.3 million OE anchor; first-nine-month FY2026 gross profit fell $10.173 million year over year
audit_findings.mechanism: An above-cycle spread embedded in the normalized OE anchor raises every forecast cash flow and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The year-over-year increase was primarily due to higher spreads between average selling prices and raw material costs ($36.1 million), higher shipments ($7.8 million) and other material costs and adjustments ($2.8 million), partially offset by higher manufacturing costs ($2.9 million).
audit_findings.explanation: Cyclicality and spread dependence are demonstrated, while the claim that $39.3 million is above normalized OE remains unresolved. The $36.1 million spread contribution is nearly as large as the anchor, and FY2026 already shows margin reversal despite higher sales. Since the valuation ranges from $24.47 to $33.65 per share around a $31.26 market price, a materially lower cycle-normalized anchor could change the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Build a full-cycle unit-spread, shipment and utilization normalization, including weak import-pricing periods, calculate the resulting OE anchor, and rerun all scenarios if it is below $39.3 million.

audit_findings.title: A retirement-benefit claim ahead of common equity is absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $12.231 million FY2025 unfunded projected benefit obligation, with zero plan assets; $0.61 per diluted share, or 2.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unfunded obligation not already captured through projected cash benefit payments is a claim deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The accumulated benefit obligation was $ 11.3 million and $ 11.4 million as of September 27, 2025 and September 28, 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The unfunded obligation is demonstrated, although whether a bridge deduction would duplicate pension costs already retained in OE requires reconciliation. Even deducting the entire $12.231 million would reduce values by about $0.61 per share: 2.5% of bear, 2.1% of base and 1.8% of bull equity value. It would not change which scenarios are above or below the $31.26 price; the 30%-MOS buy threshold would decline by about $0.43 per share.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the latest SRBA obligation to deferred-compensation liabilities and verify whether forecast OE uses pension expense or actual benefit payments; deduct only the portion not already represented in forecast cash flows.

audit_findings.title: Non-operating life-insurance gains may remain in owner earnings while the underlying asset is omitted
audit_findings.magnitude: Cash-surrender-value gains were $0.452 million in FY2025, $1.532 million in FY2024 and $0.776 million for the first nine months of FY2026; the latest policy asset was $14.865 million versus $12.411 million of deferred compensation
audit_findings.mechanism: Investment gains affect historical OE and its trend anchor, while the policy asset and economically related compensation or retirement claims affect the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The cash surrender value of life insurance policies increased $452,000 in the current year compared with $1.5 million in the prior year due to the corresponding changes in the value of the underlying investments.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that the gains entered reported earnings and that the asset is outside the stated bridge, but the supplied record does not establish whether the OE calculation purged the gains. Removing gains would lower OE, while separately recognizing the policy asset could raise the bridge; related deferred-compensation obligations complicate the net effect. The inconsistent treatment may affect value, but materiality cannot be established without the historical OE workbook and liability matching.
audit_findings.action: Trace cash-surrender-value gains and losses through every historical OE calculation, identify the obligations economically supported by the policies, and rerun using either a fully purged operating treatment plus the net policy asset in the bridge or a consistently integrated treatment.

audit_findings.title: Stripped deal and restructuring costs may be recurring at the corporate-strategy level
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 restructuring and acquisition costs totaled $2.629 million; first-nine-month FY2026 restructuring costs were $0.051 million and acquisition costs were zero
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back recurring acquisition and integration costs raises normalized OE, while excluding future purchase consideration can make acquisition-dependent growth appear costless.
audit_findings.evidence: Looking ahead, we will continue to evaluate acquisition opportunities that enhance our presence in markets we currently serve or expand our geographic footprint.
audit_findings.explanation: The FY2025 add-backs are relevant, but the record does not demonstrate recurring annual costs: charges fell to $0.051 million in the next nine months and the identified consolidations were substantially completed. Continued acquisition evaluation is forward-looking. The issue becomes valuation-relevant if forecast growth depends on additional acquisitions without their execution costs and purchase consideration.
audit_findings.action: Track acquisition, integration, relocation and closure spending by deal; identify whether the 3% or 6% growth assumptions require acquisitions, and rerun with normalized deal costs and purchase consideration if acquisitive growth is credited.

audit_findings.title: The perimeter record omits the OWP acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: OWP purchase price was $5.116 million, equal to 0.9% of the $576 million base equity value; acquired revenue and earnings are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The omission affects perimeter metadata, acquisition adjustments and the trigger for replacing partial-year history with a first-full-year observation, but not current as-filed OE.
audit_findings.evidence: On November 26, 2024, we, through our wholly-owned subsidiary, IWP, purchased certain assets of OWP for a purchase price of $ 5.1 million.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter-record error, not a demonstrated numerical error in the present valuation. FY2025 as-filed earnings already include OWP after November 26, 2024, and OWP-specific earnings cannot be quantified after integration. The current valuation therefore is not changed, but future supersession or comparison logic could become inconsistent if OWP remains omitted.
audit_findings.action: Add OWP and its November 26, 2024 closing date to the perimeter record, confirm that acquisition-related adjustments cover both transactions, and apply the first-full-year supersession rule consistently to EWP/LSG and OWP.
